content_units: Gentle Fantasy Picks for a 10-Year-Old

These choices fit a reader who enjoys magical worlds, quests, friendship, and wonder without leaning too dark or frightening. I prioritized age-appropriate fantasy with clear reading-level guidance and low-to-moderate intensity.
8 Recommended Fantasy Books and Series
Title   Reading Level   Complete?   One-line pitch

Nevermoor: The Trials of Morrigan Crow by Jessica Townsend   Ages 9–12; middle grade   Ongoing   A cursed girl escapes her fate and enters a dazzling magical society full of tests, secrets, and found family.
The Land of Stories by Chris Colfer   Ages 8–12; middle grade   Complete   Twins tumble into a fairy-tale world where classic characters, adventure, and humor collide.

The Girl Who Drank the Moon by Kelly Barnhill   Ages 10–13; upper middle grade   Standalone / Complete   A lyrical, Ghibli-like fantasy about a girl raised by a kind witch and the magic hidden inside her.

Kiki’s Delivery Service by Eiko Kadono   Ages 8–12; middle grade   Complete enough to read on its own   A young witch leaves home with her cat to build an independent life in a warm, whimsical seaside town.

The Wings of Fire series by Tui T. Sutherland   Ages 9–12; middle grade   Main arcs complete; series continuing   Dragon heroes go on prophecies, quests, and friendships-packed adventures in an easy-to-devour fantasy world.
Howl’s Moving Castle by Diana Wynne Jones   Ages 9–12; middle grade   Complete   A clever girl under a curse teams up with a dramatic wizard in a funny, magical, heart-filled adventure.

The Penderwicks on Gardam Street / fantasy-adjacent alternative: The Greenwild by Pari Thomson   Ages 9–12; middle grade   Ongoing   A girl discovers a hidden wilderness magic world filled with plants, mystery, and wonder.
Dragon Rider by Cornelia Funke   Ages 9–12; middle grade   Complete enough to read on its own   A silver dragon, a brownie, and a boy set off on a globe-spanning quest to find a legendary safe haven.
Best-Fit Notes for This Reader
Option 1:   Nevermoor     Most Harry-Potter-like in magical-school energy and found-family charm   Best for big-world magic
Option 2:   The Land of Stories     Fast, funny, accessible fantasy with fairy-tale adventure   Best for confident but not advanced readers
Option 3:   Howl’s Moving Castle     Strong Studio Ghibli overlap with whimsy, humor, and magic   Best for a Ghibli-loving reader
Option 4:   Dragon Rider     Quest fantasy with warm-hearted stakes and memorable creatures   Best for Percy-Jackson-style adventure
Reading-Fit Notes
-   Easiest entry points:   The Land of Stories, Kiki’s Delivery Service, Dragon Rider
-   Best if they want “magic school” vibes:   Nevermoor
-   Best for a dreamy, gentle tone:   The Girl Who Drank the Moon, Howl’s Moving Castle
-   Best for binge-reading many books:   Wings of Fire
-   Least scary overall:   Kiki’s Delivery Service, The Land of Stories, Howl’s Moving Castle
